title: Persona panel and second opinion
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for independent second opinions before a decision: a panel of reviewers, each with a stated perspective and, where possible, a model family different from the producer's; takes given alone from the same sealed packet, with no reviewer seeing another's; an independence check before any view is read; a synthesis that leads with where the reviewers disagree and routes each disagreement, never by a vote; an audit by someone who wrote none of it; and a person who decides. It reuses the taste palettes and evaluation design packs where they overlap.
boundaries: Each reviewer works alone from the same packet; no reviewer sees another's view before all are sealed.
Perspective cards are roles, never real people; no one is imitated or claimed to be represented.
Reviewers spend only their workers' own allowances; this pack grants no spending and calls no model itself.
The synthesis decides nothing; only a person decides.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for independent second opinions from a panel of stated perspectives

value.lets_workers: Get second opinions before a decision: define a panel of independent reviewers, each with a stated perspective and, where possible, a model family different from the producer's; have each give a take alone from the same sealed packet, with no reviewer seeing another's; check that independence before anyone reads the views; write a synthesis that leads with where the reviewers disagree and where each disagreement goes next; have someone else audit it; and leave the decision to a person.
value.not_for: Choosing between finished options by taste, which the taste palettes pack does, or measuring which option is better, which the evaluation design pack does. A panel routes such disagreements to them.

flow.when: The plan or draft, the decision it informs and who produced it.
Each reviewer alone, as a separate attempt.
The sealed views, read in the fixed order.
Someone who wrote none of it checks the quotes and routes.
A person decides, or decides later.
A factual disagreement gets an evaluation.
A disagreement of taste becomes a palette.

value.worked_example: Synthetic: a literacy program's plan, drafted by a model run, to replace paper sign-in sheets with tablet check-in. Three reviewers on three families, one shared with the producer and labeled, take it alone. Their sealed views disagree on a fact, whether check-ins survive a site's evening wifi outages, and on a value, whether quicker check-in is worth a screen some learners cannot read. The program director proceeds with changes and leaves the factual question to a week-long test.

nouns.title: How a panel gives independent takes and a person decides
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: define-panel records the producer and its model family, picks three to five perspective cards, gives each reviewer a family, and fixes the shared packet, the deadline and the reading seed.
give-view runs once per reviewer as a separate attempt, each sealed on submission.
check-independence confirms every view used the packet, was sealed in time and names no other reviewer, before anyone reads them.
synthesize-disagreements reads the views in the fixed order and leads with where they disagree.
audit-synthesis, by someone who wrote none of it, rechecks every quote and route.
decide is a person's: proceed, proceed with changes, do not proceed or decide later.
rules: Independence is the point: a view written after reading another is a second copy, not a second opinion.
Disagreements are the output; agreement among reviewers who share blind spots is weak evidence.
A factual disagreement is settled by evidence, a value disagreement by the person, a taste disagreement by a palette and a scope disagreement by asking the requester.
Each reviewer spends only its worker's own allowance; this pack grants no spending.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

nouns.title: Guardrail: every take is independent

value.rule: Each reviewer works alone from the same sealed packet: the artifact, the question and its own perspective card. No reviewer sees another's take, the producer's view of its own work or a draft synthesis until every take is sealed.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every view names the packet digest it read and its seal time, and the independence check finds no view naming another reviewer and none read before all were sealed.

nouns.title: Guardrail: the synthesis leads with disagreement
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A synthesis leads with where reviewers disagree, quoting each side from the sealed views, and keeps a point only one reviewer raised at full weight. Agreement gets a short list, and a head count never settles a disagreement.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every disagreement quotes each position from its view, and the summary holds no majority verdict.

nouns.title: Guardrail: reviewers on other model families where possible
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Reviewers run on a model family other than the producer's wherever one is available, and on more than one family across the panel. A reviewer on the producer's family is named with the reason, and the synthesis calls that part of the panel correlated.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every reviewer's family is recorded beside the producer's, and every same-family reviewer has a stated reason.

nouns.title: Who sits on a panel
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same request and allowance give the same panel shape.

rules: Three to five reviewers, each with a different perspective card; at least one looks for how the plan fails and one stands for the people it serves.
A perspective is a role, never a real person and never an imitation of one.
The producer, whether a person or a model run, is not on its own panel, and neither is the synthesizer.
Record the producer's model family and each reviewer's. Prefer families other than the producer's, and more than one across the panel; a reviewer on the producer's family needs a stated reason.
Reviewer ids are opaque, such as r1 and r2, so an id says nothing about a perspective or a family.
Each reviewer is a separate attempt with its own lease and an execution report naming the exact provider and model.

nouns.title: Keeping the takes independent
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same views and seed give the same check and order.

rules: Every reviewer gets the same packet: the artifact by digest, the question and the instructions; only the perspective card differs.
The packet leaves out the producer's view of its own work and every other reviewer's take.
Reviewers share no conversation, memory, cache or scratch space.
A view is sealed by the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON when submitted, and nobody reads any view until all are sealed or the deadline passes.
A late view is kept and marked late. A view that names or quotes another reviewer is excluded and redone, because its independence is lost.
Views are read in ascending order of the SHA-256 of the seed, a colon and the reviewer id, so their order does not depend on who finished first.

relations: A recorded shuffle, so position does not decide.

nouns.title: Synthesizing where reviewers disagree
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same views give the same structure.

rules: Lead with disagreements. Quote every side exactly from the sealed views, with the reviewer id and perspective.
Name each disagreement's kind and route, and say what would resolve it.
Keep agreements to a short list, and list every point only one reviewer raised.
Never settle a disagreement by counting reviewers; a count is information only, with the panel size.
Say plainly when there is no disagreement, and why it may be real or correlated.
The synthesis recommends nothing; a person decides.

kinds.factual: Evidence or a measurement could settle it: route to an evaluation.
kinds.value: It turns on what matters more: route to the person who decides.
kinds.taste: It turns on preference between versions: route to a taste palette.
kinds.scope: Reviewers assumed different goals or limits: route to the requester.

verbs.title: Define a panel of independent reviewers
verbs.summary: From the plan or draft under review and the decision it informs, record who produced it and on which model family, pick three to five perspective cards, give each reviewer a family other than the producer's where one is available, and fix the shared packet, deadline and reading seed.
verbs.outcome: A panel, with one give-view verb proposed per reviewer.

slots.name: artifact
slots.description: Pin of the plan, draft or proposal under review.

slots.name: request
slots.description: Pin of the requester's question: the decision the panel informs.

steps: Verify the pins, and record who or what produced the artifact and its model family.
Pick perspective cards that differ, including one that looks for how the plan fails and one for the people it serves; write a new card in the same shape only when none fits.
Give each reviewer a family other than the producer's where the worker's allowance offers one, and name any same-family reviewer with the reason.
Fix the packet digest, a deadline and a reading seed, and propose one give-view verb per reviewer, each a separate attempt.

acceptance.check: The panel validates against template.panel's schema.
producer.on_panel is false and no reviewer is the producer.
Every reviewer has a model family, and each one matching the producer's has a same_family_reason.
No two reviewers share a perspective.

verbs.title: Give one independent view
verbs.summary: As one reviewer, read only the shared packet and your perspective card and give your own take: a stance, the points behind it with how sure you are of each, and what would change your mind.
verbs.outcome: One reviewer's view, sealed on submission.

slots.name: artifact

steps: Verify the pins, that the packet digest matches the panel's, and that you did not produce the artifact.
Read nothing but the packet and your card: no other view, no draft synthesis and no record of the producer's own assessment.
Give a stance and up to ten points from your perspective, each with why and how sure you are, and say what would change your mind.
Submit once, with saw_other_views false only when that is true; the view is sealed by its digest.

acceptance.check: The view validates against template.view's schema.
packet_sha256 equals the panel's packet_sha256.
The submitting key is not the producer's or another reviewer's.
The points follow from the card's perspective, not a generic review.

verbs.title: Check the views' independence before anyone reads them
verbs.summary: Before any view is read for its content, confirm that each used the panel's packet, was sealed before the deadline and names no other reviewer, record each view's digest, exclude any whose independence is lost, and fix the reading order from the seed.
verbs.outcome: An independence check that passes or says why not.
steps: Verify the pins, and compute each view's SHA-256 over its canonical JSON.
Compare each view's packet digest with the panel's and each seal time with the deadline, marking late views.
Scan each view for other reviewers' ids and perspectives without weighing any view; exclude one that names or quotes another and propose a fresh give-view for that reviewer.
Order the reviewer ids by the SHA-256 of the seed, a colon and the id, and pass only when at least three independent views remain.

result is passed only when same_packet and all_sealed_before_reading are true, no included view names another reviewer and at least three remain.

verbs.title: Synthesize where the reviewers disagree
verbs.summary: Read the sealed views in the fixed order and write a synthesis that leads with where reviewers disagree: each side quoted exactly with its reviewer and perspective, the kind of disagreement and where it goes next, then a short list of agreements and every point only one reviewer raised.
verbs.outcome: A synthesis that decides nothing, with palette briefs for disagreements of taste.

slots.name: independence_check
slots.description: Pin of the passed independence check.

steps: Verify the pins; end blocked when the independence check did not pass, and confirm you neither produced the artifact nor wrote a view.
For each disagreement, quote every side exactly from its sealed view, name its kind and route, and say what would resolve it.

Propose the evaluation design pack's design-evaluation verb for a factual disagreement and write a palette brief for one of taste; a value disagreement goes to the person and one of scope to the requester.
List agreements briefly and every single-reviewer point; never turn a count of reviewers into a verdict, and run the panel checks before submitting.

acceptance.check: The synthesis validates against template.synthesis's schema.
The synthesis passes every check in panel-checks.
Every quote appears exactly in its reviewer's sealed view.
Every point in every view appears in a position, an agreement or a single-reviewer point.

verbs.title: Audit the synthesis (someone who wrote none of it)
verbs.summary: A worker or person who neither produced the artifact, wrote a view nor wrote the synthesis checks every quoted position against its sealed view, looks for dropped points, disagreements sent the wrong way and head-count language, and passes the synthesis only when none is found.
verbs.outcome: A synthesis audit that passes only with nothing found.
steps: Verify the pins and that you wrote none of the artifact, the views or the synthesis.
Find every quote in its reviewer's sealed view, character for character.
List every view point the synthesis dropped, every disagreement routed against the kind rules and every sentence that settles something by a count.
Pass only with every list empty; propose a fresh synthesize-disagreements verb otherwise.

acceptance.check: The audit validates against template.synthesis-audit's schema.
positions_checked equals the number of positions in the synthesis.
passed is true only when every list in the audit is empty.
The auditing key differs from the producer's, every reviewer's and the synthesizer's.

verbs.title: Decide, having read the disagreements (a person)
verbs.summary: A person reads the synthesis and its audit and decides: proceed, proceed with changes, do not proceed or decide later, saying how each disagreement was settled or what comes next for each one left open.
verbs.outcome: A person's decision on the synthesis.
steps: Run the checklist, reading the disagreements first.
Settle each disagreement or leave it open with its next step; settle one of taste through the taste palettes pack's record-choice verb. Deciding later is valid.

acceptance.check: The decision validates against template.decision's schema.
Every disagreement id in the synthesis is in settled or left_open.
The submitting key belongs to a person who neither produced the artifact, reviewed it nor wrote the synthesis.
